correctness.rationale: For all n>=3 and m>=2n the cross-polytope support complex is explicit. A direct hitting-number argument verifies a maximal p_n-face for every support; its integral dual cocycle pairs diagonally with the sphere cycles, so the lattice is primitive. The determinant of the signed complementary-pair representation at a transposition is (-1)^(binom(2n-2,n-1)/2), with 2-adic valuation of the central binomial coefficient equal to popcount(n-1). The sign criterion and character follow. Finite exact checks corroborate n=3..6 local signs and n=3..5 maximal witnesses; the full n=3 rational rank uses Feng 2026 Theorem 18. Quotient rational invariants use standard finite-group transfer. No unproved full integral torsion-freeness is asserted.

originality.rationale: The independent sphere family and lower rank bound are expressly credited to Feng–Wang 2024, and triple rational Betti ranks to Feng 2026. The new result computes their actual integral symmetry action, exhibits the binary power-of-two orientation transition for all n, and derives natural symmetric-group quotient nonvanishing. The inspected primary texts and searched records do not contain this representation. Possible unindexed equivalents remain a risk.
residual_risks: A differently formulated or unindexed equivariant computation of the same stabilizer character could exist.
The reported triple rational rank depends on Feng (2026), which is mathematically cited as a theorem but not independently re-proved here.
For n>=4 the displayed submodule need not exhaust degree p_n homology, and the free summand does not rule out torsion elsewhere.

value.rationale: For arbitrary subset size n this describes a natural, primitive integral submodule in a high-dimensional Kneser independence complex, with a sharp and unexpected binary-arithmetic dependence of its orientation. For n-1 not a power of two it forces topological nonvanishing in the quotient by the full ground-set symmetric group. For triples it gives the entire rational degree-nine character, substantially more information than Betti numbers alone.
